all_upheld_flag: Not all upheld: 1 overturned (nested_text). For every program I worked out stdout from the source and §7.3.13 myself before opening the .out. numeric_literal_operand: checked each arm against §7.3.6.3 GR3 truncation (1.5+0 -> 1, 3.7+0 -> 3, 7/2 -> 3), checked that -1.5 is a signed literal (§8.8.1 requires a space after an operator), and checked that the fixed-point literals are allowed (§7.3.3 SR10). A literal-as-expression implementation would print A-WRONG-1 and E-WRONG-1. boolean_operands: computed every bit pattern by hand under §8.8.2 7)b) precedence NOT>AND>XOR>OR. The C and E decoys equal the left-to-right results (0110), so precedence is pinned. copy_replace: checked the §7.2.1 step order (conditional compilation in step 2, REPLACE later), so the REPLACE in the omitted WHEN OTHER cannot take effect. An implementation that leaked it would print OMITTED-REPLACE on the last line. alnum: 'ABC ' vs 'ABC', 'abc', 'AB ' vs 'AB', and N'XY ' are each separated only by GR7. fmt2: checked that the compilation variable may stand in for a literal (§7.3.11.4 GR1), that a later TRUE WHEN and WHEN OTHER are omitted, and that '=' is allowed for non-numeric literals (§7.3.8.2 1)a)2). Ran cite.py --check myself on all 17 quoted citations: all OK. Minor notes, not overturned: (1) copy_replace labels the GR4 closing paragraph as '4) b)', which is what cite.py prints. (2) GR9/GR10 are word-for-word GR5/GR6, so cite.py resolves them to 5)/6). The header's top line names GR9/GR10 correctly and the annotation says so. Found the overturn by checking every directive in the omitted paths for syntactic legality under §7.2.1.
